notes: 50-item Subprofessional Numerical batch. All source items in the supplied upload were checked for keyed arithmetic, option uniqueness, explanation alignment, distractor mapping, metadata, and repository overlap. 49 uploaded items passed this Astra content review after corrections; replacement Item 926051 remains draft/unreviewed because it was authored during the review. Uploaded geometry Item 926037 was valid but held outside this batch so the requested allocation is 12 fractions, 12 percentage items, 8 ratio/proportion, 8 basic algebra, and 10 age/work/distance/money/mixture word problems. It is preserved separately as a held draft. Target times now follow CSE-Question-Design-Spec §3.1 by archetype. The resulting 50-item draft-batch mean is 69.3 seconds; do not administer this authoring batch as a single timed practice set until set-level pacing is redesigned. Difficulty mix is 11 easy, 25 medium, 14 hard versus the spec suggestion of 15/25/10; labels are editorial, not empirically calibrated. Repository similarity screening covered 3,333 unique stems from current main and 10 pinned content PR snapshots; no >=0.65 stem match, within-batch match, or stable-ID collision was found. This is not a comparison to the source reviewer PDFs. The existing qa_file.py still crashes on the fraction archetype because its solver assumes a narrow "had <number>" stem. No question was imported or activated. Only reviewed items remain not approved for users; a separate GT approval is still required before any release or activation. Item 926003 uses NUM-WRONG-BASE as the nearest available code for fraction-comparison heuristics; the spec has no dedicated numerator-only/denominator-only comparison code.

items.micro_skill: subtract a quarter from an eighth-based measure
items.stem: A small fish pond was 7/8 meter deep. Maintenance lowered the water by 1/4 meter. What was the new water depth?

reveal.terms: To subtract fractions, first make their denominators match.
reveal.shortcut: Change 1/4 to 2/8. Take away 2 eighths from 7 eighths: 7/8 − 2/8 = 5/8.
reveal.why_correct: 5/8 meter is right because raising the final level by 1/4 meter returns it to 7/8 meter.

why_wrong.o2: 1 1/8 meters adds the 1/4-meter change instead of subtracting it from the pond depth.
why_wrong.o3: 3/4 meter subtracts only the top numbers and keeps eighths; 1/4 is actually 2/8.
why_wrong.o4: 1 1/2 meters wrongly subtracts denominators; the part sizes must first match.

items.micro_skill: take a fractional part of a whole number
items.stem: Of 72 seats in a municipal training room, 3/8 are reserved for visitors. How many visitor seats are reserved?

reveal.terms: Three eighths means three of eight equal shares.
reveal.shortcut: Divide 72 by 8 to find one share: 9. Then multiply 9 by 3: 27 seats.
reveal.why_correct: 27 is correct. Eight groups of 9 make 72, and three groups make 27.

why_wrong.o1: 45 seats is the unreserved portion, not the visitor seats.
why_wrong.o3: 24 seats divides by the numerator 3 instead of finding one eighth and taking three.
why_wrong.o4: 9 seats counts one eighth and stops before taking three eighths.

items.micro_skill: compare rational numbers with unequal denominators
items.stem: A health worker filled four identical containers to 4/7, 5/9, 7/12, and 3/5 of their capacity. What fraction is the fullest?

reveal.terms: The fullest container has the greatest fraction, not the largest numerator.
reveal.shortcut: Compare each with 3/5 using cross multiplication. For 7/12, compare 7 × 5 = 35 with 3 × 12 = 36; 3/5 wins. The others are smaller too.
reveal.why_correct: 3/5 is greatest: it equals 0.6, while 7/12, 4/7, and 5/9 are each below 0.6.

why_wrong.o1: 7/12 chooses the largest numerator, but its value is only 35/60.
why_wrong.o2: 4/7 may look larger because 7 is a smaller denominator, but it is below 3/5.
why_wrong.o4: 5/9 is less than 3/5: cross-products are 25 and 27, so the second fraction is larger.

items.micro_skill: convert a mixed number to an improper fraction
items.stem: A field notebook records a measured distance as 2 3/7 kilometers. Which improper fraction represents the same distance?

reveal.terms: A mixed number has a whole part and a fractional part.
reveal.shortcut: Two wholes equal 14/7. Add 3/7, giving 17/7.

why_wrong.o1: 5/7 adds the whole number 2 to the numerator 3, then keeps the denominator 7. Each whole must first be changed to sevenths.
why_wrong.o2: 11/7 subtracts the extra 3 seventh-parts from the two wholes instead of adding them.
why_wrong.o3: 14/7 accounts for the two whole kilometers but drops the extra 3/7.

items.micro_skill: count equal portions of fractional size
items.stem: A bakery has 6 kilograms of flour for 3/4-kilogram sample bags. How many full sample bags can it fill?

reveal.terms: To count bags, divide total flour by flour in one bag.
reveal.shortcut: Divide 6 by 3/4. Turn division into multiplication by 4/3: 6 × 4/3 = 8.
reveal.why_correct: Eight bags use 8 × 3/4 = 6 kilograms exactly.

why_wrong.o2: 2 bags treats each bag as 3 kilograms and ignores the denominator 4.
why_wrong.o3: 24 bags counts quarter-kilogram portions but forgets that each bag holds three such portions.
why_wrong.o4: 6 bags repeats the flour amount without dividing by the size of one bag.

items.concept: recover the whole from a fraction
items.micro_skill: divide a known part by its share of the whole
items.stem: A relief team counted 45 blankets on one shelf. That shelf held 5/8 of all the blankets. How many blankets did the team have?

reveal.terms: The whole equals a known part divided by the fraction it represents.
reveal.shortcut: Five equal parts contain 45 blankets, so one part has 9. Eight parts have 9 × 8 = 72.
reveal.why_correct: 5/8 of 72 is 45, exactly the shelf count.

why_wrong.o1: 45 is only the count on the shelf, not the full supply.
why_wrong.o3: 9 blankets is one part of the eight-part total, before multiplying by eight.
why_wrong.o4: 120 blankets divides by the missing 3/8 share rather than the stated 5/8 share.

items.micro_skill: divide a mixed-number volume by a fractional cup size
items.stem: A nutrition volunteer has 1 1/2 liters of juice. Each serving is 3/8 liter. How many equal servings are possible?

reveal.terms: A serving count is total volume divided by volume per serving.
reveal.shortcut: Convert 1 1/2 to 12/8 liters. Each serving takes 3/8, so 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
reveal.why_correct: Four servings use 4 × 3/8 = 12/8 = 1 1/2 liters.

why_wrong.o1: 12 servings counts eighth-liters but forgets that each serving needs three eighths.
why_wrong.o2: 3 servings assumes every serving takes half a liter instead of 3/8 liter.
why_wrong.o4: 6 servings incorrectly treats each serving as 1/4 liter.

items.micro_skill: combine quantities with different fractional parts
items.stem: A farmers' cooperative collected 1 2/3 kilograms of bean seeds from one plot and 2 1/6 kilograms from another. What was the combined weight?

reveal.terms: Convert fractional parts to the same denominator before adding.
reveal.shortcut: 2/3 is 4/6. Add 4/6 and 1/6 = 5/6. Add the whole numbers 1 + 2 = 3.
reveal.why_correct: 3 5/6 kilograms is correct because 1 2/3 + 2 1/6 = 3 5/6.

why_wrong.o1: 4 5/6 kilograms counts one extra whole kilogram.
why_wrong.o2: 3 1/2 kilograms subtracts fractional parts instead of combining them.
why_wrong.o3: 3 1/3 kilograms adds the fractional numerators and denominators separately, which changes the part size.

items.micro_skill: find the unfinished share when parts use the same whole
items.stem: A coastal cleanup crew finished 3/10 of a shoreline on Saturday and another 1/5 of the same shoreline on Sunday. What fraction remains?

reveal.terms: The remaining part is one whole minus the portions already finished.
reveal.why_correct: 1/2 remains. Half was cleaned, so the other half is left.

why_wrong.o2: 1/10 subtracts Sunday’s completed part from Saturday’s instead of finding what is left from one whole.
why_wrong.o3: 7/10 stops after Saturday and ignores Sunday’s cleanup.
why_wrong.o4: 4/5 counts only Sunday’s work and forgets Saturday.

items.micro_skill: simplify a three-place decimal
items.stem: A rain gauge showed 0.625 of its maximum capacity. Which fraction in simplest form is equal to 0.625?

reveal.terms: Three digits after a decimal point mean thousandths.
reveal.shortcut: Write 0.625 as 625/1000. Divide both by 125 to get 5/8.
reveal.why_correct: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625. Both values describe the same part of the gauge.

why_wrong.o1: 8/5 reverses 5/8, making a number bigger than 1 although 0.625 is below 1.
why_wrong.o3: 25/4 shifts the decimal place by using hundredths rather than thousandths.
why_wrong.o4: 5/16 divides the correct fraction by 2 a second time.

items.micro_skill: take successive shares of a collection
items.stem: A nursery has 45 seedlings. Two thirds are native trees, and 3/5 of those native trees are narra. How many narra seedlings are there?

reveal.terms: “Of those” means the second fraction applies to the smaller group.
reveal.shortcut: First take 2/3 of 45 = 30 native seedlings. Then take 3/5 of 30 = 18 narra seedlings.
reveal.why_correct: 18 is correct: 18 of 30 native seedlings is 3/5, and 30 of 45 seedlings is 2/3.

why_wrong.o1: 27 seedlings takes 3/5 of the entire nursery instead of only the native trees.
why_wrong.o2: 9 seedlings first uses the nonnative one-third rather than the two-thirds of native trees.
why_wrong.o4: 30 seedlings counts all native trees before selecting only the narra.

items.concept: multiply a mixed number by a fraction
items.micro_skill: find a fractional part of a mixed distance
items.stem: A rural footpath is 2 2/3 kilometers long. Surveyors have measured 3/4 of it. How many kilometers have they measured?

reveal.terms: “Three-fourths of” means multiply by 3/4.
reveal.shortcut: Change 2 2/3 to 8/3. Multiply 8/3 × 3/4; cancel the 3s to get 8/4 = 2.
reveal.why_correct: 2 kilometers is three-fourths of 2 2/3 kilometers because 2 ÷ (2 2/3) = 3/4.

why_wrong.o1: 2 2/3 kilometers is the full footpath, not the measured three-fourths.
why_wrong.o2: 0.75 kilometer treats the entire footpath as only one kilometer.
why_wrong.o3: 3 5/12 kilometers adds a fraction to the path length instead of taking a fraction of it.

items.micro_skill: calculate fifteen percent by parts
items.stem: An Albay library received 360 donated notebooks. It set aside 15% for an outreach class. How many notebooks were set aside?

reveal.terms: Percent means per hundred. Fifteen percent is 15 out of every 100.
reveal.shortcut: Find 10% of 360 = 36. Half of that is 5% = 18. Add 36 + 18 = 54.

why_wrong.o2: 72 notebooks is 20% of 360. It treats the requested 15% as 20%, adding an unsupported five percentage points.
why_wrong.o3: 36 notebooks calculates only 10%, leaving out the additional 5%.
why_wrong.o4: 24 notebooks divides the total by 15 instead of taking 15 hundredths.

items.micro_skill: convert part over whole to percent
items.stem: At a Davao orientation, 18 out of 60 invitees came by bicycle. What percentage of invitees came by bicycle?

reveal.terms: Percentage of a group equals part ÷ whole × 100.
reveal.shortcut: Divide 18 by 60 to get 3/10. Then 3/10 × 100 = 30%.
reveal.why_correct: 30% of 60 = 18, so the answer matches the reported bicycle riders.

why_wrong.o1: 3 1/3% reverses part and whole and does not multiply the fraction by 100.
why_wrong.o3: 18% repeats the attendee count as a percent without dividing by the 60 invitees.
why_wrong.o4: 70% describes the people who did not cycle, not the 18 who did.

items.micro_skill: find the total when twenty-five percent is given
items.stem: A municipal registrar has encoded 72 documents, which is 25% of the assigned files. How many files were assigned in total?

reveal.terms: Twenty-five percent is one fourth of the whole.

why_wrong.o2: 72 files is the already encoded quarter, not the complete assignment.

items.micro_skill: subtract a one-eighth discount from a listed price
items.stem: A bicycle repair cooperative lists a helmet at ₱800 and offers a 12.5% discount. What is the sale price?

reveal.terms: A discount lowers the original price. 12.5% equals one eighth.

reveal.why_correct: The ₱700 sale price plus ₱100 saved returns the ₱800 list price.

why_wrong.o1: ₱720 assumes a 10% discount rather than the stated 12.5%.
why_wrong.o2: ₱100 is the amount saved, not the price the buyer pays.

items.micro_skill: measure change using the original total as base
items.stem: A ferry carried 240 passengers on Monday and 300 on Tuesday. What was the percentage increase in passengers?

reveal.terms: Percent increase means extra amount divided by the old amount.
reveal.shortcut: The ferry gained 300 − 240 = 60 passengers. Divide 60 by 240 = 1/4. Convert to 25%.
reveal.why_correct: 25% of 240 is 60; adding 60 to 240 gives 300.

why_wrong.o2: 60% uses the number of extra passengers as if it were already a percentage.
why_wrong.o3: 125% measures Tuesday’s full total relative to Monday, not the increase alone.
why_wrong.o4: 20% divides by Tuesday’s new total. Percent increase uses Monday’s original 240.

items.micro_skill: combine completed counts before computing a rate
items.stem: At a vocational fair, 80% of 20 morning attendees completed a survey. In the afternoon, 60% of 30 attendees completed it. What percentage of all attendees completed a survey?

reveal.terms: To combine different-sized groups, first count successes in each group.
reveal.shortcut: Morning: 80% of 20 = 16 surveys. Afternoon: 60% of 30 = 18. Together 34 of 50 completed a survey, so 34 ÷ 50 × 100 = 68%.
reveal.why_correct: 68% of 50 is 34, matching the 16 + 18 completed surveys.

why_wrong.o1: 70% averages the two rates equally even though the sessions have different numbers of attendees.
why_wrong.o3: 34% confuses the 34 completed surveys with a percentage of 50 attendees.
why_wrong.o4: 32% is the percentage who did not complete the survey, not those who did.

items.micro_skill: find a percentage close to the whole
items.stem: A records office verified 72 of 80 marriage-certificate entries. What percentage has been verified?

reveal.terms: The completed percent is completed ÷ total × 100.
reveal.shortcut: 80 − 72 = 8 not yet checked, which is 10% of 80. Thus 100% − 10% = 90% verified.
reveal.why_correct: 90% × 80 = 72 verified records, exactly as stated.

why_wrong.o1: 8% confuses the 8 unverified records with a percentage.
why_wrong.o2: 10% is the unverified portion, since 8 entries still need checking.
why_wrong.o4: 80% simply repeats the total count as a percent; 72 is the part to compare with 80.

items.concept: compare a percentage discount with a fixed rebate
items.micro_skill: subtract savings to see which is larger
items.stem: A shuttle ticket costs ₱600. Offer A cuts 20% off; Offer B gives a flat ₱90 rebate. How much more does Offer A save than Offer B?

items.micro_skill: find a named share after summing ratio parts
items.stem: A community workshop has red and blue stools in a ratio of 4 to 7. There are 55 stools in all. How many stools are blue?

reveal.terms: A 4-to-7 ratio means 4 equal parts red and 7 equal parts blue.
reveal.shortcut: There are 4 + 7 = 11 parts. One part is 55 ÷ 11 = 5. Blue stools: 7 × 5 = 35.
reveal.why_correct: 35 blue and 20 red stools total 55; their counts have the ratio 7 to 4.

why_wrong.o2: 11 stools counts the total number of ratio parts as if each part were one stool.
why_wrong.o3: 20 stools is the red share of four parts, not the blue share of seven.
why_wrong.o4: 5 stools is the value of one part before multiplying by seven.

items.micro_skill: scale both sides of a given ratio
items.stem: A rural collection center stores coffee beans and cacao beans in a 5-to-8 ratio by sack count. If there are 30 coffee sacks, how many cacao sacks are there?

why_wrong.o3: 30 sacks simply repeats the coffee count, assuming equal counts instead of the 5-to-8 ratio.
why_wrong.o4: 6 sacks is one ratio part; cacao requires eight such parts.

items.micro_skill: undo an addition to isolate an unknown
items.stem: A supply log shows that a delivery contained 17 folders more than the morning count. The delivery count was 49 folders. How many folders were counted in the morning?

reveal.terms: To undo “17 more,” subtract 17 from the new amount.
reveal.shortcut: Let the morning count be x. Then x + 17 = 49. Subtract 17: x = 32.
reveal.why_correct: 32 + 17 = 49, so 32 is the missing earlier count.

why_wrong.o2: 66 folders adds the extra 17 rather than removing it from 49.
why_wrong.o3: 49 folders is the later delivery count, not the earlier count.
why_wrong.o4: 17 folders is just the increase, not the morning quantity.

items.micro_skill: undo multiplication after opening parentheses
items.stem: A craft set includes three identical bundles. Each bundle contains some beads and four spacers. Across the three bundles there are 45 pieces. How many beads are in each bundle?

reveal.terms: Each bundle has x beads plus four spacers, so three bundles mean 3(x + 4).
reveal.shortcut: Write 3(x + 4) = 45. Divide by 3 to get x + 4 = 15. Subtract 4: x = 11.
reveal.why_correct: Three bundles of 11 beads and 4 spacers contain 3 × 15 = 45 pieces.

why_wrong.o1: 33 beads counts all beads across three bundles, not in one bundle.
why_wrong.o3: 19 beads adds the four spacers back after dividing, instead of subtracting them.
why_wrong.o4: 15 pieces is everything in one bundle before removing the four spacers.

items.micro_skill: solve for the larger of two unknown numbers
items.stem: Two delivery routes cover 68 kilometers in total. One route is 14 kilometers longer than the other. How long is the longer route?

reveal.terms: When two numbers have a sum and a difference, add both to find twice the larger one.
reveal.shortcut: Add 68 + 14 = 82. Divide by 2: 41 kilometers is the longer route.
reveal.why_correct: The shorter route is 68 − 41 = 27; 41 − 27 = 14 kilometers.

why_wrong.o1: 34 kilometers is the equal half before allowing for the 14-kilometer difference.
why_wrong.o2: 54 kilometers subtracts the difference from the total but does not split the remaining relationship.
why_wrong.o4: 27 kilometers is the shorter route, not the longer one.

items.micro_skill: find the greater of two consecutive even integers
items.stem: Two consecutive even apartment numbers add up to 78. What is the larger apartment number?

reveal.terms: Consecutive even numbers are two apart.
reveal.shortcut: Their average is 78 ÷ 2 = 39. The numbers one below and one above 39 are 38 and 40.
reveal.why_correct: 38 + 40 = 78, and both are consecutive even numbers. The larger is 40.

why_wrong.o1: 38 is the smaller even apartment number.
why_wrong.o2: 39 is the average of the two numbers, not either even apartment number.
why_wrong.o3: 42 is too high: the consecutive even pair ending at 42 is 40 and 42, which totals 82, not 78.

items.micro_skill: undo multiplication before isolating a value inside parentheses
items.stem: A training group prepares 3 identical sets of forms. Each set has x forms after 4 damaged forms are removed. If the three sets contain 24 usable forms in total, how many forms were in each set before the damaged forms were removed?

reveal.terms: Each set starts with the same number of forms. Four are removed from each set, leaving x usable forms per set.
reveal.shortcut: The 24 usable forms are shared across 3 sets: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 usable forms in each set. Add back the 4 damaged forms: 8 + 4 = 12 forms originally in each set.
reveal.why_correct: 12 forms is correct. Removing 4 from each original set leaves 8, and 3 × 8 = 24 usable forms.

why_wrong.o1: 8 forms is the number left in each set after the damaged forms are removed, not the starting number.
why_wrong.o3: 4 forms is the number removed from each set, not the number originally prepared.
why_wrong.o4: 28 forms adds the four damaged forms only once to the total of 24 usable forms, then stops before dividing the usable total among 3 sets.

items.micro_skill: subtract a fixed charge then divide by a unit charge
items.stem: A document binding shop charges ₱120 to set up an order and ₱35 per booklet. A group paid ₱400. How many booklets were bound?

reveal.terms: A fixed fee is charged once; the price per booklet applies to each booklet.
reveal.shortcut: Remove the ₱120 setup fee: ₱400 − ₱120 = ₱280. Divide ₱280 by ₱35 per booklet: 8.
reveal.why_correct: 8 booklets cost 8 × ₱35 = ₱280; with the ₱120 fee, the bill is ₱400.

why_wrong.o1: 9 booklets adds an extra booklet after correctly dividing the variable charge by ₱35.
why_wrong.o3: 3 booklets divides the ₱120 setup charge by ₱35, using the wrong part of the bill.
why_wrong.o4: 11 booklets uses the whole ₱400 as if there were no ₱120 setup charge, then rounds down.

items.micro_skill: solve for an original amount from a fractional remainder
items.stem: A recycling shop sold 12 kilograms of plastic bottles. After the sale, the remaining stock was 3 kilograms more than half the starting stock. How many kilograms did it have at the start?

reveal.terms: Let x be the starting stock. After selling 12 kilograms, x − 12 remains.
reveal.shortcut: Set x − 12 = x/2 + 3. Move half of x to the left: x/2 = 15. Double to get x = 30.
reveal.why_correct: Starting with 30 kilograms and selling 12 leaves 18; half of 30 plus 3 is also 18.

why_wrong.o1: 24 kilograms doubles the sold amount but leaves out the three extra kilograms in the remainder.
why_wrong.o2: 15 kilograms is half the original stock, not the full starting amount.
why_wrong.o4: 18 kilograms subtracts the three-kilogram remainder adjustment instead of adding it.

items.micro_skill: solve an equation with repeated unknowns and brackets
items.stem: A school exhibit uses two trays with x beads and 6 labels in each tray, plus a third bag with x beads only. Altogether there are 42 pieces. How many beads are in each tray?

reveal.terms: Two copies of x plus one more x make three copies of x.
reveal.shortcut: Write 2(x + 6) + x = 42. Remove the 12 labels: 3x = 30. Divide by 3: x = 10.
reveal.why_correct: Two trays each have 10 beads and 6 labels, plus a bag of 10 beads: 16 + 16 + 10 = 42.

why_wrong.o1: 18 beads removes labels for just one tray and divides among only two groups.
why_wrong.o2: 14 beads divides all 42 pieces by three before removing the 12 labels.
why_wrong.o3: 15 beads divides the remaining beads between two trays but forgets the third bag.

items.concept: past ages with a fixed gap
items.micro_skill: relate a past age ratio to ages today
items.stem: A speech therapist is 21 years older than a trainee. Five years ago, the therapist was four times as old as the trainee. How old is the trainee today?

reveal.terms: An age difference stays constant when both people age by the same years.
reveal.shortcut: Let t be the trainee’s age now. The therapist is t + 21. Five years ago: t + 16 = 4(t − 5). Solve t + 16 = 4t − 20, giving 3t = 36 and t = 12.
reveal.why_correct: Today their ages are 12 and 33. Five years ago they were 7 and 28, and 28 is four times 7.

why_wrong.o2: 33 years is the therapist’s age today, not the trainee’s.
why_wrong.o3: 16 years subtracts the five-year interval from the age gap instead of setting up the past age relationship.
why_wrong.o4: 7 years is the trainee’s age five years ago, not today.

items.concept: ages from future sum and gap
items.micro_skill: undo a future total before splitting ages
items.stem: Two cousins are 6 years apart. Four years from now their ages will total 48. How old is the younger cousin today?

reveal.terms: The age gap stays the same, but their combined age grows by two years each year.
reveal.shortcut: Four years from now the total is 48. Today it is 48 − 8 = 40. The younger age is (40 − 6) ÷ 2 = 17.
reveal.why_correct: Today the cousins are 17 and 23; in four years they will be 21 and 27, totaling 48.

why_wrong.o1: 23 years is the older cousin’s present age, not the younger one.
why_wrong.o3: 20 years is their current average age; the younger cousin is three years below it.
why_wrong.o4: 21 years forgets that both cousins will each be four years older at the future date.

items.micro_skill: scale output using workers and hours
items.stem: Three equally fast volunteers pack 360 relief kits in 6 hours. At the same pace, how many kits can 5 volunteers pack in 4 hours?

reveal.terms: Work output at a constant pace depends on both worker count and time.
reveal.shortcut: The first crew worked 3 × 6 = 18 volunteer-hours. Each volunteer-hour makes 360 ÷ 18 = 20 kits. New output: 5 × 4 × 20 = 400 kits.
reveal.why_correct: Five volunteers working four hours provide 20 volunteer-hours, 2 more than before, so 400 is reasonable.

why_wrong.o1: 360 kits simply repeats the production of the first crew instead of adjusting workers and time.
why_wrong.o2: 240 kits scales down to four hours but keeps only the original three volunteers.
why_wrong.o4: 600 kits accounts for five volunteers but keeps the original six-hour shift.

items.micro_skill: add job fractions completed per hour
items.stem: One pump empties a pond in 8 hours. Another pump can empty the same pond in 12 hours. If both operate together from the start, how long will they take?

reveal.terms: Two pumps working together add the parts of a pond they empty each hour.
reveal.shortcut: In one hour they empty 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24 of the pond. Total hours = 24/5 = 4 4/5 hours.
reveal.why_correct: 4 4/5 hours × 5/24 pond per hour = one whole pond. Both pumps finish faster than either pump alone.

why_wrong.o1: 10 hours averages the completion times and is slower than the faster pump alone.
why_wrong.o2: 6 hours assumes two pumps each work at the slower pump’s rate; their actual rates differ.
why_wrong.o3: 20 hours adds the individual completion times instead of adding their hourly work rates.

items.micro_skill: convert mixed hours to speed and trip time
items.stem: A provincial bus covers 72 kilometers in 1 1/2 hours at a steady speed. How many hours will it need to travel 120 kilometers at the same speed?

reveal.terms: Speed equals distance divided by time; time equals distance divided by speed.
reveal.shortcut: Speed: 72 ÷ 1 1/2 = 48 km/h. For 120 km, time is 120 ÷ 48 = 2 1/2 hours.
reveal.why_correct: 48 km/h × 2 1/2 hours = 120 km, matching the distance.

why_wrong.o2: 0.9 hour reverses the distance ratio, making a longer trip take less time.
why_wrong.o3: 48 hours mistakes the bus speed, 48 kilometers per hour, for a travel time.
why_wrong.o4: 1 1/2 hours repeats the time for the shorter 72-kilometer trip without increasing the time for the longer 120-kilometer trip.

items.micro_skill: use total distance divided by total time
items.stem: A delivery van travels 50 kilometers at 50 km/h, then another 50 kilometers at 25 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire 100-kilometer trip?

reveal.terms: Average speed is total distance divided by total travel time.
reveal.shortcut: First 50 km takes 1 hour. Second 50 km takes 2 hours. Total: 100 km in 3 hours, so 100 ÷ 3 = 33 1/3 km/h.
reveal.why_correct: At 33 1/3 km/h, three hours cover 100 km. The slower portion lowers the overall speed.

why_wrong.o1: 100 km/h repeats the total distance as if it were a speed.
why_wrong.o3: 37 1/2 km/h takes the simple average of two speeds even though the slow segment takes longer.
why_wrong.o4: 50 km/h is only the speed on the first segment.

items.micro_skill: subtract unit cost before multiplying sales
items.stem: A campus kiosk sells 18 prepaid study cards for ₱35 each. Each card costs the kiosk ₱22. What is its total profit on these sales?

reveal.terms: Profit is selling price minus cost. Total profit is profit per item times number sold.

why_wrong.o1: ₱396 is the kiosk’s cost, not the profit.
why_wrong.o2: ₱13 is the profit on one card, not all eighteen cards.

items.micro_skill: calculate cost per kilogram using total value and weight
items.stem: A rice cooperative blends 3 kilograms of grain costing ₱45 per kilogram with 2 kilograms costing ₱60 per kilogram. What is the average cost per kilogram of the mixture?

reveal.terms: A weighted average divides the total cost by the total quantity.
reveal.shortcut: First grain costs 3 × ₱45 = ₱135. Second costs 2 × ₱60 = ₱120. Total ₱255 for 5 kg. Divide: ₱255 ÷ 5 = ₱51 per kg.
reveal.why_correct: ₱51 × 5 kg = ₱255, the total purchase cost.

why_wrong.o2: ₱255 is the cost of all five kilograms, not the average cost of one kilogram.
why_wrong.o3: ₱52.50 averages the two prices without weighting them by the different kilograms.
why_wrong.o4: ₱105 adds the two price tags rather than computing a price per kilogram.

items.micro_skill: preserve dissolved amount while changing total volume
items.stem: A 20-liter salt solution is 10% salt by volume. Pure water is added until the solution is 8% salt. How many liters of water were added?

reveal.terms: Adding pure water changes the total volume but not the amount of salt already dissolved.
reveal.shortcut: Salt initially: 10% of 20 = 2 liters. After dilution, 2 liters is 8% of the whole. New volume: 2 ÷ 0.08 = 25 liters. Add 25 − 20 = 5 liters.
reveal.why_correct: The diluted 25 liters contains 2/25 = 8% salt, so adding 5 liters works.

why_wrong.o1: 2 liters is the unchanged salt volume, not the added water.
why_wrong.o3: 4 liters takes 20% of the original volume instead of using the new 8% concentration.
why_wrong.o4: 25 liters is the final volume of the diluted solution, not just the water added.
